headline: Committee hears public testimony on mayor's proposed budget from Lahaina fire survivors

meeting.body: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee
meeting.summary: At a listening session on BFED 1, testifiers raised long-term recovery funding, rental help and a Lahaina land trust request, and one objected to a $60 million increase. The chair closed testimony and adjourned; a council member will report to the next meeting.
meeting.recap: The committee held a community listening session.[[0:00:00]] The only agenda item was BFED 1, the mayor's proposed budget.[[0:05:04]] A testifier said MEO paratransit, a door-to-door bus service, changed her life.[[0:06:21]] A long-term recovery group said it has 245 families in its care and 160 more on a wait list.[[0:13:31]] A council member said the group's $500,000 request is not in the mayor's proposed budget.[[0:23:53]] A taxpayers group objected to a $60 million budget increase.[[0:28:12]] A fire survivor said his family earns $14,000 a year over the limit for an MEO rental program.[[1:05:29]] A council member said page 433 of the program budget has over $10 million for mental health.[[1:14:02]] A fire survivor said housing, not mental health spending, is the real need.[[1:15:00]] A testifier asked the council to restore $6 million in unrestricted funding for a Lahaina land trust.[[1:23:58]] The testifier also asked the council to keep $2.4 million from the Affordable Housing Fund for building homes.[[1:24:07]] The chair closed public testimony and adjourned the meeting.[[1:48:02]]
meeting.next: Council staff took notes, and a council member will report what the community said at the next meeting. The chair asked a fire survivor seeking rental help to leave his name and information with staff so they can follow up.

moments.q: "This is the first time I felt peace since the fire."
"This is our window to bring Lahaina back into Lahaina hands."

issues.brief: The testifier said recent land trust purchases cost $500,000 to $700,000 per property.[[#1]] A council member said $12 million went to Maui United Way for rental help that has not yet been given out.[[#2]] A fire survivor said 155 Hawaiian homes for Lahaina fire survivors are trying to move forward.[[#3]]
